THE FINANCIAL AUTOPSY • EDITORIAL MANIFESTO Singapore Equity Desk

"The name has a little drama to it. Most of the actual work involves reading footnotes." (Julian Lim, CFA)

Picture a company announcing record profits while its shares fall. If your first reaction is that something doesn’t quite add up, I know the feeling.

My instinct is to look at what sits behind the headline. Investors might have expected more, or the outlook might have weakened. The latest results are one part of a valuation that also depends on expectations about the future.

That instinct is why I chose the name The Financial Autopsy.

I like pulling a financial story apart and working out what produced the result. If profits rose, was the company selling more, charging more, spending less or benefiting from something unlikely to happen again? Each explanation gives me a different reason to be confident, or cautious, about what comes next.

"The name has a little drama to it. Most of the actual work involves reading footnotes."

About the Analyst

I’m Julian Lim, a financial analyst based in Singapore, a finance graduate and a CFA charterholder. Over the past ten years, my career has taken me from equity research at DBS Vickers to the investment team at Lion Global Investors, where I progressed to Senior Investment Analyst.

That experience taught me to look at an investment from several angles. A company can have an appealing product, capable management and an impressive growth plan. I still want to understand how it earns money, how much capital it needs and what expectations I’m being asked to pay for.

It also taught me that a useful explanation takes work. I’ve spent enough time with financial models to know how easily a neat spreadsheet can make an uncertain forecast look settled. When I put forward a view, I want you to understand the reasoning well enough to question it.

You might already have a portfolio. You might still be figuring out why profit and cash flow are different. Either way, you’re welcome here. I enjoy explaining how businesses work, and a thoughtful question from someone seeing a company for the first time can be surprisingly useful.

First Company Under Coverage: Broadcom ($AVGO)

My first company under coverage will be Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO). Following it will take me into the semiconductor industry, AI investment, enterprise software and the wider economic environment shaping its prospects. I’ll give the company its own introduction and develop my assessment as the research progresses.

Other companies and industries may follow. Part of the appeal of this profession is that there is always another business to understand and another investment decision to weigh. As an aspiring fund manager, I’m interested in how those individual decisions fit together, too.

The Ambition

My ambition is to launch my own investment fund, and I hope some of the people reading this will eventually become its first clients. Before that, I want to earn a regular place in your reading list. You should have time to see how I think, challenge my assumptions and decide whether my judgement deserves your confidence.

Welcome to The Financial Autopsy. I’m glad you’re here.
